title: Hot Local
statement: Implement `solve(n, binds_local)`. A loop body reads one name `n` times. `binds_local` is 1 when that name is a local variable and 0 when it is a global. Return a dict with keys `global` and `local`. The side that applies gets `n` and the other side gets 0. A local is one slot load. A global is one dictionary load. They do not both happen for the same read.
hints: If binds_local is 1, local is n and global is 0.
If binds_local is 0, swap those counts.
Do not add extra lookups for the loop counter. Count only the named read.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: CPython loads a local by index into the frame's fast locals and loads a global by a dictionary lookup on the module.

editorial: CPython loads a local by index into the frame's fast locals and loads a global by a dictionary lookup on the module. In a tight loop the same read is one or the other for every iteration. The model charges n to exactly one of the two counters.
